sub: Flat rates charge interest on the full amount for the whole term. How to read the EIR, why fees hit short loans hardest, and the four numbers to get in writing.

kicker: Same headline rate, S$10,000 over 5 years
title: Flat 3% charges nearly twice the interest
source: Our illustrative calculations, equal monthly instalments, no fees. The flat-rate loan works out to an EIR of about 5.6%.
alt: Comparison of a S$10,000 loan at 3% flat and 3% monthly rest over five years: S$1,500 of interest versus about S$781
caption: The advertised number is the same. The cost is not.

kicker: A 1% processing fee on a 3% flat loan
title: The shorter the loan, the more the fee costs
source: Our illustrative calculations on S$10,000, fee deducted upfront. Without the fee the EIR is about 5.5% to 5.7% at every tenure.
alt: Bar chart of the EIR on a 3% flat personal loan with a 1% fee: about 6.1% over five years, 6.4% over three years and 7.4% over one year
caption: A fee waiver is worth most on a short loan.

title: Past 12x your income, one door stays open.

kicker: Interest-bearing unsecured debt, in months of income
title: Which doors close, and when
source: MAS rules for banks and other regulated lenders. Only interest-bearing balances count; secured loans such as a home loan do not.

title: The caps still allow the cost to double
